C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, frozen spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. One deliverable, the reconciliation the superseded predecessor could not deliver under its own ratified criteria: in `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, the pairing test named `pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes` (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:600` at this plan's base commit) keeps its substance and loses its occupancy transcription — the `cases` table (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:602`-609) and the count comparison (`:617`) — and gains exactly the three file-determined relations the repair Goal mandates, plus the anti-occupancy guard in the house body-shaped single-definition form. One task. The record is this bundle's read, never its write (spec P4): no task re-runs the flush, the mint, or `--retire` against the production record — the end state the predecessor produced is asserted by the shipped production assertions in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (AC-END-STATE-HELD's CloseEvidence), never re-performed, and every mutation probe lives on a throwaway copy.
The red and the green (spec P1). Measured at this plan's commit `cf4e0ce` (branch `c-flush-and-pay`, tree clean apart from this bundle's own untracked artifacts): `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` exits 1 — read from the command, not a pipeline — 24 pass / 1 fail, the failure the occupancy pin at `src/artifact/xml.test.ts:617` for `findings.xml`, expected 195, received 210; `bun run test` reports 1787 pass, 3 skip, 1 fail across 63 files, the single failure this test; every other `validate:ci` stage exits 0 when run separately at this commit (typecheck, validate:cli, validate:marketplace, validate:examples, validate:determinism, validate:packed, validate:schema-reference, validate:skeleton-templates, validate:teaching-surface, validate:citation-anchors, validate:record-retirement, prove-record-preservation) — so the whole red is this one assertion and the whole repair is this one file. The repair makes that same command green: the plan's TargetAssertions carry `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` as a MustPassCommand, so the red-to-green flip of one instrument demonstrates both directions. Nothing outside the spec's write scope changes: ObservedWriteScope is exactly the repair file, and the byte-invariance commands pin every other surface to the spec's base commit `ce9b506f763fe9a97d57e10f3c3cf7b24266f277` (F210's named baseline; F215's window — the commands are this bundle's own diff, and the predecessor's supersede arrival and this bundle's own later archive arrival are named exclusions). Dated engine counts, expiring context only (F123's law): 210 / 78 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 45 / 354 by `parseGraceXmlArtifact` plus `childNodes` over direct children against the pins 195 / 77 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 44 / 338 — four stale, three agreeing, the deltas reconstructing the predecessor's committed work exactly. The pins do not go back in: no criterion, assertion, or task below carries a transcribed record element count in any form (spec P3), and the repaired test reads every number it uses about a record file from that file at test time.
T1 — granularity, one task. The budgets re-read at HEAD: `FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:187`) and `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:193`), firing per task on failed verification attempts by exact kind+key signature equality (`src/grace-cursor.ts:1824`-1835). The deliverable is one file and one failure family — the pairing test's content: a mis-stated relation reds the suite in T-001 and reds the same relation's probe on the copy, so the probe demonstrations are that family's discriminating half, not a second family. Splitting them would put a green-but-undemonstrated boundary between the repair and its probes with no isolation gain (same file, same suite, same OWS), and there is no second unrelated family here whose failures need the distinct budget held in reserve. The by-hand criterion AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE is implemented by this one task's Verification commands and the plan's TargetAssertions and carries the plan's single `Satisfies` (measured basis below).
T2 — what the deleted counts were protecting, and what already catches which part. The counts guarded wholesale record corruption that stays well-formed and pairs cleanly: a drop, a duplicate, a copy-instead-of-move, a wrong flip. Shipped instruments and their parts: the eligibility codes catch archive-paid elements still live (`finding-eligible-still-live` `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1380`, `registry-eligible-still-live` `:1399`, `decision-eligible-still-live` `:1429`); `status-file-mismatch` `:1483` catches a verbatim cross-sibling copy whose status was not made consistent (re-driven at this plan's commit: a verbatim f206 copy into the retired sibling reds it, validator exit 1; the status-flipped form of the same copy exits 0); the shipped flush invariant catches exactly-once for the sixteen flushed ids f205 through f220 (id-scoped); the shipped roots invariant asserts `base + headroom = ceiling` and `base` equal to its shipped metric for the four live roots, including the `decisions.xml` clause that relation (c) restates — the mandated set is shipped, not pruned, and the overlap is stated rather than hidden: (c) is the pairing-test-level read-back of the relation the roots invariant already asserts at the suite level, and the shipped validator alone stays green on the Entry-removal mutation because it never re-derives the persisted base against the metric (measured zero findings); the retired-layer invariant catches a retired Finding whose `PaidBy` is missing, empty, or disagrees with a derived row — and rides through a copy carrying any real archive name when the token has no derived row (measured: `F204` has no row-route payer, so a plausible `PaidBy` passes it); `prove-record-preservation` asserts body-hash presence across the genre union. Only the new relations catch: corpus-wide identity uniqueness across all seven files (duplication of any element beyond the named ids), cross-layer disjointness for non-eligible, status-consistent copies — the shipped validator measured green on exactly that copy — and, at the pairing surface where the counts used to live, the base read-back. The plan adds no second copy of any shipped end-state assertion (the spec's NonGoal): its assertions are the shipped suite commands, and the three relations are exactly the spec's mandated set.
T3 — the suites' root binding, and what it permits and forbids for probes. The pairing test resolves the production record from its own tree — `path.resolve(import.meta.dir, "..", "..", "docs", "plans", "active", "RM-GOVERNED-PATH")` (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:601`) — and the retirement suite from `REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(import.meta.dir, "..")` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:18`); neither takes a record path; only the shipped CLI does (`validateRecordRetirement({ repoRoot, recordDir })`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1296`). Consequence, binding on every probe below: a standalone copy of the record is invisible to both suites, so suite probes run on throwaway REPOSITORY copies with the copy's record mutated and the suite run inside the copy, while the CLI probes (the `--retire` no-op, the plain validator) take a standalone record copy. The AC-END-STATE-HELD red direction and every AC-OCCUPANCY-REPLACED mutation therefore run as repository copies; the spec's own Assumption 6 records this resolution, and this plan states it as the operative rule rather than rediscovering it.
T4 — assertion wiring. BaselineAssertions carry the shipped end-state instruments that are green before the write — the retirement suite (67 pass / 0 fail / exit 0 at this plan's commit) and the shipped validator (exit 0) — plus `MustExist` for the repair file, the retirement suite, the seven record files and the spec; they red if the end state this bundle asserts is broken before work starts, or if any asserted file is missing. TargetAssertions carry the repair's own suite — the same command that is red at baseline — plus the end-state suite, the validator, and the two record validators; the red-to-green flip of `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` is the demonstration of P1's both directions, and it reds at target if a relation is missing or weakened to a subset, a pairing breaks, or a transcribed count returns (the guard). The byte-invariance commands are task `Verification` and close-only `CloseEvidence` instruments (`git diff --exit-code` with a named baseline — F210), never TargetAssertions, in the predecessor's house shape.
T5 — the execution/close boundary. The executor emits this task's own execution-time cursor events (opened with the epoch open at this task's start, progress, attempt on every verification cycle, command-run events from the target lint's `--run-commands`, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected) inside the open epoch, and does not omit them. Close acts, owned by the authority and performed by no task: the terminal event, the cursor fold, `--assertions final --run-commands`, the review verdicts, gate apply, the `status="applied"` write, gate archive, the git mv to `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, the close's own record retirement move — a byte-level no-op here, because no `Row` in either registry layer carries `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` (measured by parse at this plan's commit, so both the close's move and a fresh `--retire` over a throwaway copy of the end state report moved 0) — and the CloseEvidence evaluations recorded on the post-archive Verdict (F196's applied-archive state). The predecessor's supersede is already committed (`cf4e0ce`); this bundle performs no outward-facing act.
The one `Satisfies`, and why. The approved spec's evidence-hygiene Constraint reads "no task carries `Satisfies`, the admissible mapping set is empty, and every criterion is complete `CloseEvidence` except the by-hand one". Measured at this plan's commit with the shipped engine over the real approved spec: a plan with no `Satisfies` leaves AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE — the by-hand criterion, which carries no `CloseEvidence` child — unmapped, and `validateSpecPlanCoverage` emits warning `change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2058`-2064); AC-CLOSE-LINT's post-archive command runs `--fail-on warnings`, which fails on any issue (`src/grace-lint.ts:142`-143), so the literal reading makes the bundle's own close unsatisfiable. The house pattern is the predecessors' own: every ratified bundle in this lineage that carried this by-hand criterion mapped exactly it via `Satisfies` (`C-PAYMENT-RECORD`, `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2`, `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3`, `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`, `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` — searched at this plan's commit). This plan therefore carries exactly one `Satisfies` — AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE under T-001 — a criterion that is not close-bound, so `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` cannot fire, while the close-bound criteria stay unmapped because a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is that error; the admissible mapping set for the close-bound criteria is empty, exactly as the spec states. The same engine returns zero coverage issues with this mapping (driven both ways at this plan's commit).
Scalar expiry and probe timing. Every dated figure below and in the criteria is plan-time context that expires on the next record or suite write (F123); every criterion asserts a relation its instrument can observe, and no criterion pins a record element count. The five AC-OCCUPANCY-REPLACED probes wait for the repair, because the relations do not exist until T-001's edit lands — the spec drives its own probes at its base commit and delegates exactly these to this plan, demonstrated during execution on throwaway repository copies with the repaired suite run inside each copy, tails recorded in the executor's report before the authority accepts the delivered work and runs the close.

T-001.Title: Replace the occupancy transcription in the pairing test with the three file-determined relations and the anti-occupancy guard, and demonstrate every named probe on throwaway copies

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The repair, in `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` only. The pairing test named `pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes` keeps its substance: the record-directory resolve from its own tree (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:601` — the root binding is unchanged, T3), all seven real record files parsed at their committed bytes with the shipped `parseGraceXmlArtifact`, a non-null root per file, `computeElementSpans` succeeding so every loud disagreement still raises (source-scan/parser count disagreement, parsed attribute outside its open-tag bytes, self-closing open tag with parser children, non-self-closing element without a close tag), a span for every direct genre child, index `Entry` elements self-closing, and the explicit generous timeout kept (F185). It loses the `cases` table (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:602`-609 at this plan's base commit) and the count comparison (`:617`) — the `expected` column and every other transcribed element count of a record file — and gains exactly the three relations the repair Goal mandates, no more and no fewer: (a) identity — every direct genre child of the seven files carries its genre identity attribute (`Finding` id, `Decision` id, `Row` name, `Entry` id) and the identities are unique within their file; (b) conservation — for the findings, rulings and registry genre pairs the live and retired identity sets are disjoint; (c) index bookkeeping — the `decisions.xml` root's persisted `base` equals the count of its direct `Entry` children with `layer="live"`, read back through `parseGraceXmlArtifact` and `childNodes` (the `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` live-entry metric). Measured green at this plan's commit, expiring figures (F123): identity 0 missing and 0 duplicate across the seven files (210 / 78 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 45 / 354 direct genre children), disjointness 0 overlap in all three pairs, `decisions.xml` root `base="271"` equal to its 271 live `Entry` children — the criteria bind the relations, never the figures, and every number the test uses about a record file is read back from that file at test time. The per-file genre tag stays the test's existing local pairing shape (the file-to-tag mapping is pairing substance, not a count). No occupancy pin returns in any form — not as the `expected` column, a constant, or an inline literal (spec P3); if any relation proves non-assertable at implementation time, stop and report rather than reintroducing a count.

The anti-occupancy guard, in the same file, in the house body-shaped single-definition form. A second shipped test reads the file's own source — the regression-guard shape of `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1586`-1594, which reads its own source via `import.meta` and runs a keyed scan over it, refusing what it cannot prove — and expects an empty failure list. The scan observes that the pairing test carries no transcribed record element count in any form, keyed on the three forms the spec names: (i) any numeric literal inside the pairing test's body span — the relations need none, so a restored `expected` column, an inline literal, or an in-body count constant dies there; (ii) the occupancy-table shape anywhere in the file — an `expected: number`-shaped field on a record-file table, the triple-array form the deleted table took; (iii) any module-scope binding whose initializer is a numeric literal or a numeric-literal array and which is referenced from the pairing test's body — the constant form. Keyed shapes only; the guard may be strengthened at implementation, never weakened; the mutation that reddens it is restoring any transcribed count in the pairing test's body, demonstrated per the probe criterion below.

The discriminating probes, driven during execution — never against the production record. Every suite probe runs on a throwaway copy of the REPOSITORY with the copy's record mutated and the suite run inside the copy, because neither shipped suite takes a record path (T3); CLI probes take a standalone record copy. (0) The end-state red direction, on a repository copy: the unmutated copy runs `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` green (67 pass / 0 fail / exit 0 at this plan's commit — re-drive the control and record the tail); with `F205` replanted live in the copy's `findings.xml` and its `<PaidBy>` dropped from `findings-retired.xml`, the same suite exits 1 with the flush, payment, roots, production and clamp invariants among the failures (driven at the spec's base: 60 pass / 7 fail / exit 1 — re-drive and record the tails). (1) Duplicate one `Finding` element in a copy's `findings.xml`: identity uniqueness (a) reds in the repaired pairing test run inside the copy. (2) Copy one live `Finding` element into the copy's `findings-retired.xml` as a well-formed retired element — status flipped to `retired`, nothing deleted: the shipped validator alone stays green (measured exit 0 on exactly this mutation at this plan's commit) and the disjointness relation (b) reds on the same bytes; the verbatim (status-kept) form is caught by the shipped `status-file-mismatch` first (measured exit 1) and discriminates nothing, which is why the status-consistent form is the demonstrated one. (3) Remove one live index `Entry` from a copy's `decisions.xml`: the base read-back (c) reds, and the shipped validator stays green because it never re-derives the persisted base against the metric (driven at the spec's base: zero findings after the removal) — while the shipped roots invariant reds at the suite level on the same mutation, relation (c) being its pairing-surface restatement. (4) Restore any transcribed count in the repaired test inside a copy: the anti-occupancy guard reds. (5) The growth probe — append one fresh, well-formed `<Finding>` (house shape, fresh id, not archive-paid) and its `<Entry>` to a copy's `findings.xml` and `decisions.xml` and re-persist the copy's live roots exactly as the next flush's wave would: findings `base` = `newlineCount` read back from the written file, index `base` = the live-`Entry` count read back, `headroom` = ceiling minus base, ceiling byte-identical and never raised — the predecessor T-001's ratified root procedure — and every relation stays green, which is the discrimination any restored count lacks. Each mutated copy has its unmutated twin run green in the same instrument, so a refusal discriminates rather than merely fails; every tail lands in the executor's report.

The by-hand rule and the boundary. This task's `Verification` commands and the plan's `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root, checked by hand (F171, the shipped detector missing the `grace.ts` form): no `Command` text contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes lint of this root omitting `--assertions`; current-mode lint appears only as the post-archive `CloseEvidence` of AC-CLOSE-LINT. This task carries the plan's single `Satisfies` (AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE) — the mapping the close's `--fail-on warnings` requires (measured basis in the IntentSummary); the close-bound criteria stay unmapped, because a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is the error `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied`. The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events for this task (opened with the epoch open at this task's start, progress, attempt on every verification cycle, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected) inside the open epoch and does not omit them; the terminal event, the cursor fold, the `--assertions final --run-commands` gate, the review verdicts, gate apply, the `status="applied"` write, gate archive, the archive move, the close's own record retirement move — a byte-level no-op here, no `Row` carrying `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` — and the `CloseEvidence` evaluations are close acts owned by the authority; no task performs any of them, and no sentence in this plan implies execution does. Do not hand-write any status. No task re-runs the flush, the mint, or `--retire` against the production record (spec P4): the record is this bundle's read, never its write, and no task boundary sits anywhere the record is not byte-identical to the spec's base commit. The `lint --change C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2 --assertions target --run-commands` command is the post-write evidence command and is meant to run during execution with an open cursor on a declared task; its exit 1 today (pre-approval, `assertion.change-not-approved` — driven at this plan's commit) is not a defect (F184's refined rule: a recorded `Verification` command must exit 0 at the stage it is meant to run, and a plan is not judged by running its execution-stage commands at plan time).
